thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPEN — Private connectivity alerts from monitoring: elevated DNS timeouts and TCP resets for PrivateLink endpoints in us-east-2 (AZB). Severity: P2. Pager sent to oncall.
alice (oncall): paging in. seeing customer-reported errors for ACME corp - can't reach internal api over privatelink from their VPC.
acme-support: they opened a ticket at 04:02 UTC, multiple sessions timed out. Provided traceroutes showing packets stall at our AZB egress.
maria (sre): checking metrics — spike in DNS ERR responses from resolver pool backing privatelink-us-east-2b. Query latency up from 12ms to 600ms.
jay (netops): BGP feeds show route churn between AZA reflector and AZB spine around 03:58 UTC. Looking at control-plane logs.
alice (oncall): can we confirm if it's DNS only or also TCP path failures for the same endpoints?
maria (sre): from packet captures on lb-edge-us-east-2b: seeing UDP retrans and TCP three-way handshake resets. Correlates to same time window.
jay (netops): running show ip bgp neighbors — one path flapped: bgp-peer 10.10.43.21 keepalive timeout, then rapid re-advertise. Possible hardware or microburst causing route withdrawal and re-add.
acme-support: customer says ~30% of requests fail, mostly short-lived but enough to cause job retries.
alice (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) steer traffic away from AZB for ACME by adjusting routing policy to prefer AZA replicas; 2) add temporary DNS failover TTL change? 3) engage infra to check fabric in AZB.
tim (platform): can do canary steering — create route policy for their tenant id to prefer AZA endpoints. pushing rule now: /api/v1/routing/steer --tenant acme --prefer az=a
deploy-bot: route policy update applied (change-id: rp-1778a). Will take effect in ~15s for new flows.
jay (netops): also we pushed a BGP dampening to peer 10.10.43.21 to reduce flap effect while we investigate.
maria (sre): lowering resolver TTLs for privatelink zone to 30s to hasten client failover. Pushing change to dns-control plane.
alice (oncall): acme - can you confirm if retries decreased after we steered?
acme-support: initial reports: error rate dropped ~60% after steering. Some sessions still hit AZB for existing connections.
alice (oncall): good. next: get hardware telemetry from AZB TOR and spine. @jay any low-level alarms?
jay (netops): TOR telemetry shows microburst 1Gbps on interface TenGigE0/1 between leaf-43 and spine-7 at 03:57-04:01. Queueing caused packet drops which explains TCP resets and DNS timeouts.
alice (oncall): route bounce + microburst => transient control-plane instability. Who can coordinate rack-level patching if needed?
jay (netops): opening fabric ticket with on-site ops. They will check transceivers and buffer config. ETA 30m for physical check.
tim (platform): for short term, recommending aggressive connection-level retries on our side for PrivateLink session managers and increase TCP SYN retrans timeout to reduce perceived errors.
maria (sre): ramping additional resolver capacity in us-east-2b to absorb jitter. Also enabling prefix caching at edge to avoid additional lookups.
acme-support: customer appreciates the fast steering; they asked for an estimated time to full resolution.
alice (oncall): initial RCA points to inter-AZ egress microburst causing BGP withdraws. Mitigations: routing steer to AZA, bgp dampening, TTL reduce, resolver capacity ramp. Target: customer-facing errors <1% within 15m, full fabric validation by ops in 30-60m.
incident-bot: oncall handoff scheduled: alice -> maria at 04:30 UTC. Please post status for handoff.
alice (oncall): handing off to Maria. Summary: steered acme traffic to AZA (rp-1778a), resolver TTL lowered, bgp dampening enabled, ops investigating AZB hardware microburst. ACME error rate down to ~8% from 30%. I'll leave runbook steps in #incidents-runbooks.
maria (sre): picked up. I'll keep this incident active, monitoring ACME metrics and fabric ticket updates. Can someone paste the traceroute and tcpdump snippets used earlier?
jay (netops): pasting snippets:
```
traceroute to privatelink.acme.internal (10.200.5.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.3 ms
 2  10.10.43.1  1.2 ms
 3  10.10.43.21  * * *
 4  10.10.100.7  35.8 ms
```
```
# tcpdump -n -i eth1 host 10.200.5.12 and port 53
04:00:12.123456 IP 10.20.3.5.51234 > 10.200.5.12.53: UDP, length 64
04:00:12.123789 IP 10.200.5.12.53 > 10.20.3.5.51234: UDP, frag 0
04:00:13.234000 IP 10.20.3.5.443 > 10.200.5.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
04:00:13.234500 IP 10.20.3.5.443 > 10.200.5.12.443: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0
```
```
# bgp summary | grep 10.10.43.21
10.10.43.21   4   03:57:09    Idle (administratively reset)
```

maria (sre): thanks. I'll keep collecting logs. Reassigning on-call pages to net-ops for fabric fix once ops confirms hardware check.
acme-support: customer confirms error rate at ~2% now for new requests. They've paused batch jobs for 20 more minutes, will re-enable if stable.
alice (oncall): adding note: do NOT change peering ACLs unless coordinated with net-ops; we've seen risk of sticky sessions.
maria (sre): noted. Plan for next 60m: 1) watch metrics for two TTL cycles (2 mins), 2) confirm ops hardware checks, 3) remove routing steer only after stability window of 30m.
jay (netops): ops on-site confirmed flaky SFP on leaf-43 port TenGigE0/1; replaced module and tested. Immediate telemetry shows normalized queue depth.
alice (oncall): great. can we roll back bgp dampening and steering once stable test window passes?	im (platform): prepared rollback: /api/v1/routing/steer rollback rp-1778a; will wait for SRE signoff.
maria (sre): rolling monitoring window started at 04:18 UTC. Current ACME errors: 0.7% over last 5m.
acme-support: customer re-enabled batch at 04:25 UTC; no errors so far.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — Mitigation applied, customer traffic steered, hardware replaced in AZB leaf. Monitoring. Severity downgraded to P3.
alice (oncall): closing handoff summary for my shift. Tags: privatelink, azb, bgp-flap, sfp-replace. I'll file follow-up with netops for RCA doc.
maria (sre): I'll keep incident open until 05:00 UTC for final verification, then mark resolved. Will add notes to the incident tracker.
jay (netops): RCA draft: faulty SFP causing microburst and BGP instability -> traffic steering and dampening prevented broader impact. Recommend SFP health checks and improved queue monitoring thresholds.
alice (oncall): thanks team. postmortem owner: jay. Please include timeline + action items.
acme-support: sending thanks from customer; they'd like a short summary for their compliance team.
maria (sre): will prepare customer-facing summary and internal postmortem. Closing updates will be posted in this thread.
